summary: Created SettingsViewModel with 5 constructor parameters (ISettingsService, IThemeService, IDatabaseConnectionStore, ObfuscationSettingsViewModel, IFolderPickerService).

Implemented all 5 tab observable properties: General (MySqlBinaryFolder, ExternalXmlEditorPath, VlcExecutablePath, UseVlc), Database read-only (ActiveConnectionHost, ActiveConnectionDatabase, ActiveConnectionUsername), Thumbnails (ThumbnailSize, KeepOriginalSize), Appearance (SelectedTheme, SelectedLanguage), Logging (Verbosity). ObfuscationVm is a read-only injected property.
LoadAsync: calls private PopulateFromSettings(), then GetActiveAsync() for DB tab, then ObfuscationVm.LoadAsync().

SaveCommand: builds AppOptions snapshot via with { } chains; calls ISettingsService.SaveAsync; calls IThemeService.SetAsync when SelectedTheme != _loadedTheme (IncludeCancelCommand=false to avoid spurious CancelSaveCommand).
CancelCommand: calls PopulateFromSettings() only — does not reload ObfuscationVm.
BrowseMySqlFolderCommand: calls IFolderPickerService.PickFolderAsync; no BrowseVlcPathCommand or BrowseXmlEditorCommand declared.
Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

comments.note: SettingsViewModel.PopulateFromSettings() is a private helper called by both LoadAsync and CancelCommand. This sharing prevents any drift between the two paths — a good pattern to preserve. Future maintainers adding new settings properties must update PopulateFromSettings(), not just LoadAsync, or CancelCommand will silently not revert the new field.

The Database tab properties (ActiveConnectionHost/Database/Username) are populated only during LoadAsync, not during CancelCommand (PopulateFromSettings only touches ISettingsService.Current fields). This is intentional — the database tab is read-only so there is nothing to revert. However, if the active connection changes while the Preferences page is open, the displayed values will be stale until the page is reloaded. A brief note in the View about this intended behavior would prevent confusion.

SettingsViewModel has no tests. The ViewModel logic is straightforward (property mapping + save/cancel) but the SaveCommand theme-change guard (_loadedTheme tracking) and the CancelCommand no-ObfuscationVm-reload contract are both observable behavior that warrant unit tests in VideoIndexer.App.Tests. WP-009 has no QA test scope per the active pipeline stages, so this is deferred work.

summary: WP-009 code review: FAIL — one Blocking issue found in SaveCommand.

SaveCommand does not update _loadedTheme after SaveAsync succeeds. If the user saves (applying a theme change) and then makes another theme change and saves again without navigating away (triggering LoadAsync), the second save will skip SetAsync — IThemeService will be stale while the settings file is correct. Fix: `_loadedTheme = SelectedTheme;` after SaveAsync.

All other aspects are clean: constructor null guards correct, PopulateFromSettings() DRY pattern is well-designed, with { } immutable update chain is correct, CancelCommand does not reload ObfuscationVm, BrowseMySqlFolderCommand is correct, zero warnings confirmed.

comments.note: BLOCKING — Logic bug in SaveCommand: _loadedTheme is not updated after SaveAsync succeeds. This causes a stale baseline for subsequent saves in the same page session. Repro: (1) Open settings page — LoadAsync sets _loadedTheme = Dark. (2) Change SelectedTheme to Light, click Save — SetAsync(Light) is called correctly, but _loadedTheme is still Dark. (3) Change SelectedTheme back to Dark, click Save — SelectedTheme (Dark) == _loadedTheme (Dark), so SetAsync is NOT called — but IThemeService is still showing Light. Result: theme in the settings file is correct but the live theme (IThemeService) is stale until the page is reloaded. Fix: add `_loadedTheme = SelectedTheme;` immediately after `await _settingsService.SaveAsync(updated, cancellationToken);` in the Save() method. This aligns the tracked baseline with the just-persisted state so future saves in the same session compare against the correct reference point.

AC#4 is marked met by QA but the underlying condition is not fully correct: the AC text says 'when SelectedTheme differs from the value loaded during LoadAsync' — as written, this is what the implementation does. However, the intended semantics should be 'when SelectedTheme differs from the last saved/loaded value' to prevent the stale-theme bug described above. After the fix (_loadedTheme = SelectedTheme post-save), AC#4 will be satisfied under both the literal wording and the correct intent.
